about: p05-ipc queue targets (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p05-ipc.md, section 6). scripts/cmux-next/ipc-census.py --record writes `base`; --check fails when a queue grows past it or an allowlist entry has no reason or matches no site. Allowlist entries are {queue, file, key (optional: the whole file), reason}. Task p05-ipc-106 adds the transient daemon connections of section 3.1. `ipc5_ops` lists the IPC-5 ops; cmux-tui/scripts/bench-daemon-latency.py `--ops all` measures each of them and refuses to run when one has no plan. `runtime.Q16` (items {file, line, key, p95_ms, wire}) and `runtime.Q16_run` (command, scenario, threshold_ms, sha, host, daemon_version, skipped, failed) are written by `bench-daemon-latency.py --ops all --scenario scale --write-q16` on a macOS fleet host (p05-ipc-002); ipc-census.py reads Q16 from there. p05-ipc-128 recorded the Q9 run: `runtime.Q9` (items {file, line, key}, read by ipc-census.py for Q9 and Q18) and `runtime.Q9_run` (sha, host, command, runs); `triage.Q9` gives every (kind, site) of that run a `task` (`tasks.Q9` defines the p05-ipc-3NN ones; others are existing tasks), a `reason`, or both; `why` holds the backtrace that ties a site to its task. p05-ipc-136 recorded Q18: request_path record lines carry `op=` (the request watchdog names each request), `runtime.Q18` holds every (sqlite site, op) pair of that run and `runtime.Q18_run` how it ran; ipc-census.py reads Q18 from `runtime.Q18`. `triage.Q18` gives each pair of an IPC-5 op the registry read under it (`read`) and a child task, `tasks.Q18` defines them (p05-ipc-401..407); op-less detector-test pairs are allowlisted.

Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the browser host's provider socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: another cmux app's control socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the stale-file probe of the app's own control socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the Tasks owner (cmux task serve).
Not a Q8 thread: spawn_cloud_reader_with passes the closure the name machine-agent-cloud-reader-{generation}.

The typed funnel itself: it sends a generated ResourceRequestLine through DaemonConnection's one resource request path (p05-ipc-045).

Q15.note: p05-ipc-029 re-recorded only Q15, grouped by schema family (spec/sdk-schema.json families; the method id's high byte). terminal-io (026) and tabs (029) are generated by cmux-ipc build.rs from crates/cmux-ipc/server-families.json, so server.rs writes none of their variants. Q9_run.host: cmux-orchestrator-1 (Linux 7.0.0-1014-gcp x86_64, 360 cores), debug test build
Q9_run.command: cd cmux-tui && CMUX_TUI_REQUEST_PATH_IO=record cargo test -p cmux-tui-core 2>&1 | grep REQUEST_PATH_IO | sort | uniq -c

runs.what: the command as written: lib tests
runs.result: 83 sites. 207 lib tests failed and cargo stopped before the integration targets; the 8 server::capabilities::ipc_grant_tests hang on Linux and were killed after every other test ended.

runs.what: each test binary on its own (lib minus ipc_grant_tests, and the 20 tests/*.rs targets)
runs.result: 165 sites, a superset of the first run's. With the thread blocking detector panicking (its Debug default), mux-line-out panics at server/outbound_batch.rs:57 (condvar-wait), which fails most socket tests before their handlers run. In record mode all 20 integration targets pass and the lib has 3245 passed, 246 failed, 14 ignored.

Q9_run.notes: Linux run: proc_scan sites read /proc here, sysctl or proc_pidinfo on macOS, at the same call sites. lock_hold_over_1ms depends on timing, so a fleet run can show a different subset of the sqlite sites. Backtraces for the non-sqlite sites come from CMUX_TUI_REQUEST_PATH_IO=panic:<kind> runs with RUST_BACKTRACE=1.

Q18_run.host: cmux-orchestrator-1 (Linux 7.0.0-1014-gcp x86_64, 360 cores), debug test build
Q18_run.command: cd cmux-tui && CMUX_TUI_REQUEST_PATH_IO=record cargo test -p cmux-tui-core 2>&1 | grep "REQUEST_PATH_IO kind=sqlite" | sort | uniq -c

runs.what: each test binary on its own (lib minus server::capabilities::ipc_grant_tests, and the 20 tests/*.rs targets), as p05-ipc-128 ran Q9
runs.result: lib 3392 passed, 121 failed, 14 ignored; all 20 integration targets pass. 117 (sqlite site, op) pairs over 98 sites; the site set equals runtime.Q9's sqlite sites except two lines that moved by one (server.rs:2640 -> 2641, session_event_stream.rs:485 -> 489).

runs.what: the same run on a copy whose request_path printed one backtrace per first (sqlite site, op); never committed
runs.result: lib 3393 passed, 120 failed, 14 ignored. 138 traces: the registry read (or store lock, or pin) under every pair, in triage.Q18[].read. Its record lines add two pairs the first run missed (terminal_archive.rs:69 and :201 under close-surface); runtime.Q18 is the union of both runs.

Q18_run.notes: Q18 keeps the pairs whose op is an IPC-5 op (ipc5_ops) and the op-less pairs (detector tests, which open their own unnamed scope; allowlisted). ipc5_ops_not_reached are ops no cmux-tui-core test drove through a named request scope here; the B3 bench (bench-daemon-latency.py --ops all --stress) is their record. triage.Q18 gives each kept pair the registry read under it and a child task (tasks.Q18, one per workspace_registry file) or a reason; also_serves on a task lists the non-IPC-5 ops that hit the same read.

Q18.title: Q18 resource_store.rs: resource-patch replay and the topology snapshot from memory
Q18.change: Reads WorkspaceRegistry::replay_resource_patch (resource_store.rs:924, `resource_mutations`) and resource_topology_snapshot (resource_store.rs:1436, the full topology). Every resource-patch commit (select-tab, move-tab, create-tab-group, ungroup-tab-group via commit_resource_mutation_plan; the tab-strip, rename, dock and ratio ops too) first looks its mutation up in SQLite. Add `resource_mutations` to p05-ipc-132's mutation-ledger cache (a third KeyedLedger: newest rows seeded at open, admitted entries kept until answered) and answer the replay from it; a key older than the cache replays in the writer's in-transaction check, as 132 does for the workspace and terminal ledgers. Serve resource_topology_snapshot (the interrupted-creation rollback at unpublished_creation.rs:41, machine.get/list) from p05-ipc-133's admitted overlay's newest view and, with nothing admitted, from a registry-owned topology projection seeded at open and replaced at each admit. Chromium answers the same way: IndexedDB's transaction coordinator decides conflicts in memory (content/browser/indexed_db/indexed_db_transaction_coordinator.cc), LevelDB reads the memtable before the tables (third_party/leveldatabase/src/db/db_impl.cc, DBImpl::Get).
Q18.acceptance: Golden test: after N seeded random resource mutations (commits, replays, rollbacks, a reopen), the cached replay answer and the projection equal what SQLite returns for every key and for the topology. A Q18 record run has no sqlite site for these two reads under the IPC-5 ops; request_path_io.sqlite == 0 for select-tab, move-tab, create-tab-group, ungroup-tab-group.
Q18.test_phase: RUST(resource_store); RUST(mutation_ledger); Q18 record run (p05-ipc-136 test_phase)

Q18.title: Q18 effect_store.rs: creation recovery and effect receipts from an in-memory receipt index
Q18.change: Reads resource_creation_recovery (effect_store.rs:522, `resource_creation_receipts`) on every creation (new-tab, create-terminal, split, workspace.create, pane.split; new-workspace, new-screen, new-browser-tab) through reconcile_interrupted_resource_creation, and lookup_resource_effect (effect_store.rs:255, `resource_effect_receipts`) on every effectful topology op (close-surface; workspace.close, undo-layout, notify, terminal.close, session.shutdown) and lookup_resource_creation (creation_lookup.rs:19). Keep a registry-owned receipt index: creation receipts in state executing with an effect (the only rows recovery acts on) keyed by correlation key, and the newest effect receipts keyed by idempotency key (bounded like 132's ledger cache; an older key replays in the writer's in-transaction check). Q18.title: Q18 a registry pin notes sqlite where its flow runs a statement, not at the fence
Q18.change: Site resource_router/topology.rs:299 under workspace.create (topology_operation.rs:74 lock_state_pinned) and, off the IPC-5 ops, the commit_state, close-effect and with_resource_projection pins: RegistryConnection::pin notes sqlite when the registry -> state fence is taken, and every read under it is a re-entry that notes nothing. After p05-ipc-133 a pin with every admitted entry on the overlay waits for no writer, so the fence is not I/O and the reads under it are hidden. Note sqlite at the first statement a pinned flow runs, at that statement's caller (#[track_caller] through the pinned connection), as Chrome's ScopedBlockingCall marks the blocking call, not the lock (base/threading/scoped_blocking_call.h). Then re-record and append the reads this uncovers to Q18 with a task each.
Q18.acceptance: request_path_tests: a pin whose flow runs no statement notes nothing; one that does notes once at the statement's caller; lock_hold_over_1ms still times the pin. Q18 lists the uncovered reads with tasks; no pin site remains.
Q18.test_phase: RUST(request_path); RUST(registry_connection); Q18 record run (p05-ipc-136 test_phase)
